newsitem.title: CANADA: Caledonia updates Zambia cobalt find.
newsitem.headline: Caledonia updates Zambia cobalt find.

text.p: Caledonia Mining Corp said on Thursday it has updated its estimates for its Anomaly C cobalt oxide discovery at the company's Nama project in Zambia.
The new estimates of come from a recently completed wide-spaced drilling program, the company said.

Drilling outlined an inferred mineral resource of 245 million tonnes of cobalt grading 0.030 percent, with a cutoff grade of 0.015 percent. Previous estimates at this cutoff level showed 218.9 million tonnes grading 0.029 percent.
At a cutoff grade of 0.030 percent, drilling outlined 83.7 million tonnes grading 0.051 percent cobalt, up from 73.8 tonnes grading 0.047 percent.
At a cutoff grade of 0.050 percent cobalt, drilling showed 29.6 million tonnes of ore grading 0.079 percent cobalt, up from 27.5 million tonnes grading 0.068 percent.

The updated numbers from Anomaly C increase the total indicated and inferred resources for the company's four anomalies at Nama to 875 tonnes at 0.029 percent cobalt equivalent, up from the previously announced 849 million tonnes at 0.029 percent cobalt, Caledonia said.
Anomaly C remains open at depth over a large area. ((Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100))
